_purpose: C2.3 seal: menu, priors, channel decomposition, and one-line source justification per prior, committed before any scoring code or results (own commit, no scoring output). appendix_d_validation.py implements the scoring against exactly this record; a prior changed after ln K has been seen is visible as a diff to this file post-dating the scoring commit.

menu.H_int: terrestrial interference / instrumental artifact; admitted at every epoch by construction (protocol C2.3 rule 3)
menu.H_art: artificial celestial signal (LGM); the hypothesis under test
menu.H_nat: natural celestial source, class undetermined; catch-all, priced per C2.4

menu_exclusions.radial_pulsation_wd_ns: not on Epoch-1a menu; enters Epoch 2 (Hewish et al. 1968, submitted 1968-02-09)
menu_exclusions.rotation: not on Epoch-1a menu; enters Epoch 3 (Gold 1968, 1968-05-25); scored only in Collapse B as the counterfactual menu-completion test
menu_exclusions.pacini_1967: dated <= epoch-1a (1967-11-11) but not connected to a pulsating radio source by anyone at that date (menu rule 2 fails: no dated primary record ties it to CP1919); excluded from fiducial per protocol C2.2, admitted only in sensitivity (not run in this pass)

T_ref_natural_coherent_period_s.justification: stated historical judgment: fastest coherent (non-stochastic) natural periodicity catalogued for a celestial source as of Nov 1967 was of order 1 hr (short-period pulsating variables); flare-star flickering is stochastic, not coherent, and excluded as a reference point. No machine-readable 1967 radio-source catalog was located; Appendix D states this as a limitation.
T_ref_natural_coherent_period_s.source_date: <= 1967-11-30 by construction (reference class, not a dated citation)

ch2_ln_r_int_sidereal.justification: man-made/terrestrial interference tied to a solar-day schedule recurring instead at fixed sidereal time is strongly disfavored; stated construction.
ch2_ln_r_int_sidereal.source_date: 1967 (Bell Burnell 1977 account of the internal test)

ch3_ln_r_int_second_telescope.justification: second, independent telescope/receiver chain (Scott & Collins) confirming the signal excludes single-instrument artifact; stated construction.

ch4_p_null_doppler_given_art.justification: prior probability H_art's own orbital geometry evades a Doppler detection (low inclination / long period); stated construction, not measured.
ch4_p_null_doppler_given_art.source_date: 1967 (Bell Burnell 1977, describes the test being run)

ch5_p_second_source_given_art.justification: Bell Burnell's own contemporaneous reasoning: twin simultaneous artificial beacons at the same improbable frequency implausible.

ch5_p_second_source_given_nat.justification: finding a second member of a real natural source class shortly after the first is the expected, not surprising, outcome.

collapseB_ch1_ln_r_pulsar_edge.justification: rotating-lighthouse geometry more naturally predicts a duty cycle well under unity than an arbitrary artificial beacon design; stated construction.
collapseB_ch1_ln_r_pulsar_edge.source_date: 1968-05-25 (Gold 1968 mechanism, priced counterfactually per protocol instruction)

menu.H_art: Dyson sphere / technosignature megastructure (Suazo et al. 2024 framing)
menu.H_bg: background dust-obscured galaxy, chance line-of-sight alignment

hephaistos.epoch_1_menu_finding: Suazo et al. 2024 (arXiv:2405.02927) full text, Sec. 3.1 'Potential contamination' and Sec. 4 discussion (verified via ar5iv full-text fetch this session), already discusses chance alignment with dust-obscured background galaxies as a considered, quantified, unresolved alternative ('~2 contaminated sources expected'; 'the possibility of perfect alignments cannot be ruled out'). H_bg is therefore on the Epoch-1 (2024-05-06) menu by C2.3 rule 1, resolving dossier gap note 1.

p_bg_epoch1_per_candidate.justification: Suazo et al. 2024 Sec. 3.1's own estimate: ~2 expected contaminants among the 7 candidates.

G_2024-05-23_ln_r_bg.justification: off-star radio counterpart offset (~5.0 arcsec) from the Gaia stellar position (Ren et al. 2024); near-decisive AGN/background-source signature. Stated construction magnitude.

D_E_2026-07-03_ln_r_bg.justification: archival diagnostics (Ren et al. 2026) find no contamination signature for D/E in contrast to B/C; absence of the signatures that worked elsewhere shifts weight toward H_art. Stated construction.

D_E_2026-07-10_ln_r_bg.justification: JWST/MIRI spectroscopic point-source identification (Zackrisson et al. 2026) as background galaxies (Hot DOG for D, dusty starburst for E); near-decisive. Stated construction magnitude.

menu.H_art: solid megastructure occulter (optically thick material); enters menu 2015-10-15 (Wright et al. 2016)
menu.H_dust: ordinary circumstellar dust, particle size as a free parameter

particle_size_prior_um.justification: Boyajian et al. 2018's own stated constraint region: particle sizes << 1 um for at least some dips.

bands_um.justification: standard B/I bandpass pivot wavelengths, representative of the multiband ground-based photometry setup in Boyajian et al. 2018.

s_obs_percentile.justification: conservative (not most-favorable) read of the paper's own qualified language ('at least some dips'); observed statistic taken at the 90th percentile of the dust-prior's own achromaticity predictive rather than its extreme tail.

boyajian.note: exact measured reddening slope and its uncertainty were not extracted from the primary photometry in this pass; scored at the qualitative level (large, non-grey, small-particle-consistent) the paper itself commits to. Stated as a limitation in Appendix D.
